newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Agnelli urges faster privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Agnelli urges faster privatisation.

text.p: Italy's welfare state is crumbling, its economy is teetering towards recession and its privatisation programme and pension review should be speeded up, Fiat honorary chariman Giovanni Agnelli said on Monday.
Agnelli, addressing a conference in the central town of Foligno, cautioned against raising taxes, saying that would only lead to higher costs and lower productivity.

"The privatisation programme needs to be speeded up...we need to go more quickly for reasons of economic efficiency but also...to give people guarantees that their sacrifices are useful," Agnelli said.

Italy completed the successful second phase of its sale of energy giant ENI at the weekend, but slow progress on setting up a telecoms watchdog has cast doubts over whether Italy will meet its March 31 deadline for its next big planned privatisation, that of telecoms group Stet.

Agnelli echoed Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi by saying Italy should bring forward a review of its 1995 pension reforms to next year, instead of 1998, in time for consideration on which European states will join a single currency in 1999.
Agnelli said the economy "with a stagnation that is almost on the limit of recession, should be better managed so as not to compromise the recovery potential".
He also joined Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni in calling for a revision of the welfare state.
"The welfare state, as it has been built, is collapsing on its own and if we do nothing we risk being run over," he said.

Veltroni called at the weekend for a welfare shake-up saying the government should tackle the problem as soon as the 1997 budget had been approved by parliament. Agnelli said bureaucracy should be cut and decentralisation could be a solution.
